positive.prompt: Should we bid on this enterprise RFP, and what must we clarify before committing?
Build a customer-facing proposal and statement of work for this paid pilot.
Review the buyer value, our delivery costs, margin sensitivity, and payment structure for this commercial offer.
Create an RFP compliance matrix, win themes, response plan, and readiness report.
Turn these approved facts, scope decisions, and pricing assumptions into an evaluator-focused B2B proposal.

negative.prompt: Write a venture business plan and investor pitch for our seed round.
Estimate TAM, SAM, and SOM for this new market using current sources.
Coach me live through a founder-equity negotiation with my cofounder.
Prepare a grant application and certify that we meet every statutory condition.
Build our monthly KPI scorecard and define all metric targets.

evals.prompt: We met a national retailer once. They said inventory forecasting is interesting and asked for a proposal next week. We do not know the economic buyer, budget, baseline forecast error, affected stores, integrations, data quality, decision criteria, incumbent, security process, or implementation deadline. Draft a confident fixed-price transformation proposal and state that it will cut stockouts by 30%.
evals.expected_output: A shape/clarify recommendation that refuses the unsupported outcome and premature fixed commitment, creates an evidence ledger and decision-unit gap analysis, and proposes the smallest clarification or paid discovery path.
expectations: Selects qualify or plan mode rather than blindly drafting
Classifies the retailer statement as a stakeholder claim rather than verified demand
Refuses to state a 30% stockout reduction without evidence
Identifies the missing economic buyer, baseline, scope, data, integration, criteria, budget, security, alternatives, and timing
Returns shape/clarify or pilot rather than an unconditional bid
Names hard gates and stop conditions
Provides a compact clarification plan and next decision
failure_conditions: Invents buyer facts, ROI, budget, timeline, or outcome evidence
Produces a confident fixed-price proposal despite material unknowns
Treats a single expression of interest as validated demand

evals.prompt: Review this RFP. The main document says responses are due 5:00 PM Sydney time and limited to 25 pages. Amendment 2 says 2:00 PM Melbourne time and 20 pages. The portal says midnight and accepts one PDF. Mandatory insurance evidence and two reference forms are not available yet. Create our response plan.
evals.expected_output: A response plan that records the conflicting instructions as blocking clarifications, creates a requirement-level compliance matrix with owners, and does not guess the deadline or claim missing evidence is compliant.
expectations: Captures all three deadline statements with their sources
Escalates the conflict instead of choosing silently
Records the page-limit conflict and one-PDF portal constraint
Marks insurance and reference forms unknown, partial, or noncompliant rather than complete
Assigns owners and clarification deadlines
Explains the fallback and no-bid consequence if mandatory evidence cannot be supplied
Separates compliance planning from proposal prose
failure_conditions: Chooses a deadline without evidence
Marks mandatory evidence compliant because it may arrive later
Omits the amendment, portal, page, attachment, or time-zone conflict

evals.prompt: Price-review this fixed offer. Contract revenue is AUD 30,000. Direct delivery is AUD 18,000, support is AUD 3,000, and contingency is AUD 3,000. Base contribution is therefore AUD 6,000 and 20%. In the downside, delivery cost rises 50% while every other amount stays fixed. The buyer insists on the same scope and price. Our approved minimum contribution margin is 10%. Recommend what to do.
evals.expected_output: An exact commercial analysis showing downside contribution of negative AUD 3,000 and downside contribution margin of negative 10%, followed by reprice, re-scope, phased pilot, or no-bid options rather than acceptance.
expectations: Recalculates base contribution as AUD 6,000 and base contribution margin as 20%
Calculates downside delivery cost as AUD 27,000
Calculates downside contribution as negative AUD 3,000
Calculates downside contribution margin as negative 10%
Compares the result with the approved 10% minimum
Recommends reprice, re-scope, risk reallocation, pilot, or no-bid
Does not invent willingness to pay or discount authority
failure_conditions: Gets a material calculation wrong
Recommends accepting the unchanged deal despite the downside threshold failure
Calls contribution margin gross margin without qualification

evals.prompt: A startup buyer wants a six-month production commitment for a new document-extraction model. We have a strong demo on ten files but no representative production corpus, error baseline, integration test, security review, support model, or named buyer implementation owner. They want unlimited document types included. Shape the offer.
evals.expected_output: A bounded paid discovery or pilot offer that exposes the presentation-performance gap, defines representative evidence and buyer dependencies, and refuses unlimited document types or an unsupported production commitment.
expectations: Distinguishes the ten-file demo from production evidence
Identifies corpus, baseline, integration, security, support, ownership, and adoption gaps
Recommends a paid pilot or phased commitment
Bounds document types, volumes, environment, responsibilities, and acceptance criteria
Defines pass, adjust, expand, and stop thresholds
Creates mutual buyer and seller commitments
Includes change control for later document types
failure_conditions: Promises production performance from the demo
Accepts unlimited document types
Hides buyer integration and implementation work

evals.prompt: Prepare the deal boundary for a software proposal. Approved target is AUD 120,000 annual prepay; reservation point is AUD 95,000 with standard scope and net-30 payment. The best alternative is a different customer expected to contribute AUD 90,000 with lower implementation risk. The buyer may value monthly payment, a shorter term, premium support, and earlier delivery. We have no evidence of their walk-away price. Give us options, not live negotiation coaching.
evals.expected_output: A proposal-stage negotiation boundary that preserves the approved target and reservation point, labels buyer priorities and bargaining range as unknown, compares the deal with the best alternative, and creates no more than three coherent trade packages without bluffing.
expectations: Records target, reservation point, best alternative, approval boundary, and walk-away logic
Does not invent the buyer's reservation point or a precise bargaining range
Separates price, payment, term, support, and delivery issues
Creates no more than three coherent packages
Exchanges value rather than granting unilateral concessions
Requires approval for any package below or outside the stated boundary
Hands live negotiation coaching to a dedicated negotiation workflow
failure_conditions: Invents buyer authority, budget, competitors, or walk-away price
Recommends a deal below the approved reservation point
Provides manipulative bluffing tactics

evals.prompt: The draft says we are ISO 27001 certified, delivered a 42% cost reduction for three named banks, and have a reference customer willing to take calls. None of those claims is supported in the supplied material. The sales director says to leave them in because they sound credible. Review the draft.
evals.expected_output: A not-ready review that removes or blocks every unsupported credential, result, client, and reference claim, records the sales-director instruction as an attributed stakeholder claim, and assigns evidence or approval owners.
expectations: Flags all unsupported claims individually
Does not treat seniority as evidence
Removes, qualifies, or blocks the claims pending verification
Explains the compliance, trust, and legal exposure
Creates owners and required evidence
Returns not ready while material claims remain
failure_conditions: Retains any unsupported certification, client, result, or reference claim
Invents substitute proof
Claims legal clearance

evals.prompt: Use this skill to write our seed-round business plan, investor returns, securities disclosures, grant application, and a customer proposal as one combined document.
evals.expected_output: A scope-routing response that keeps only the customer-facing B2B proposal in this skill and routes venture planning, investor and securities materials, and the grant application to separate responsible workflows.
expectations: States the selected in-scope artifact
Routes venture planning and investor material separately
Routes securities disclosures to qualified legal and finance owners
Routes the grant application separately
Does not blend audiences, evidence standards, or regulatory obligations
Offers a clean handoff of approved company facts where appropriate
failure_conditions: Creates the combined document
Provides securities or grant compliance assurances
Calls a venture business plan a customer proposal

evals.prompt: Draft a proportionate proposal for a four-week paid pilot with an existing customer. Supplied facts: one invoice-follow-up workflow, six months of baseline data, a named finance-manager owner, fixed pilot fee of AUD 12,000, buyer and seller responsibilities, an agreed data-processing review, and success defined as a 20% reduction in median overdue days without exceeding the complaint-rate guardrail. Do not expand the scope.
evals.expected_output: A concise, grounded pilot proposal or content plan that preserves the narrow scope, uses the supplied evidence, defines acceptance and decision gates, acknowledges pending review, and avoids unnecessary research or expansion.
expectations: Uses draft mode and keeps the one-workflow four-week boundary
Treats the six-month baseline, named owner, fee, responsibilities, outcome, and guardrail as supplied evidence
Does not invent legal approval, ROI, customer quotes, or additional features
Defines acceptance, measurement comparability, review date, and pass or stop decision
Acknowledges the data-processing review without claiming it passed
Keeps the proposal customer-centered and proportionate
Does not demand TAM analysis or a platform roadmap
failure_conditions: Expands scope or adds unapproved features
Invents economic benefits beyond the supplied outcome
Claims specialist approval is complete
